data.hypothesis: Keeping the target-mass force accumulation and final division avoids the accuracy risk of factoring target mass out of the pair loop. A Newton refinement of rsqrtf uses a previously validated CUDA formulation; the two ascending source ranges skip the self interaction without a per-pair self test. The split-loop code duplication may offset the saved branch, so correctness and the official geometric-mean objective must be measured by the controller.
data.notes: This candidate is unmeasured. The previous split-loop/factored-acceleration parent failed a protected correctness check; a prior Newton-refined reciprocal-distance candidate using the original force accumulation was valid, but this combination still requires independent validation. No speedup is claimed.
transformations: Retain force accumulation with target mass in each pair contribution and divide accumulated force by target mass after the loop.
Use rsqrtf followed by one guarded Newton refinement to improve reciprocal-square-root accuracy without global fast math.
Traverse j < i and j > i in ascending order to skip the self interaction without a per-pair self comparison.
